flashcards.q: Why is rebuilding an image per environment (dev/staging/prod) considered wrong even with identical source code?
flashcards.a: A rebuild re-resolves anything not pinned by digest -- an unpinned base image tag can resolve a different point release, and transitive dependencies can shift -- so identical source doesn't guarantee an identical image. Promote the same built digest via retag/copy instead of rebuilding per environment.

flashcards.q: What does ECR charge for image storage, and how much does a lifecycle policy typically save?
flashcards.a: $0.10/GB-month. A lifecycle policy pruning untagged images older than ~14 days typically cuts ECR storage 50-80% in an unmanaged repository.

Signer authenticates via OIDC; Fulcio issues a short-lived certificate binding that identity to an ephemeral keypair; cosign signs with the ephemeral key; Rekor durably logs the signature event in a transparency log. Replaces Notary v1's long-lived key management.

flashcards.q: What's the specific Kyverno misconfiguration that lets an unsigned image deploy despite a signature-verification policy existing?
flashcards.a: validationFailureAction set to Audit instead of Enforce -- the policy logs the violation but doesn't block admission. Audit mode is a legitimate rollout stage, not a steady state.

flashcards.q: What does an SBOM catch versus miss?
flashcards.a: Catches known-CVE'd direct dependencies with clean manifest metadata. Misses transitive dependencies in compiled/shaded artifacts (Java uber-jars, bundled JS) where the original dependency graph isn't statically recoverable post-build. A clean SBOM scan means 'no known CVE in what we could enumerate,' not 'no vulnerabilities.'

flashcards.q: Why attach an SBOM as a cosign attestation rather than a plain file next to the image?
flashcards.a: A signed, digest-bound attestation can't be swapped or tampered with after the fact; a plain SBOM file has no cryptographic binding to the specific image digest it claims to describe.

flashcards.q: What's the pricing model difference between ECR and Artifactory/Nexus?
flashcards.a: ECR bills storage only ($0.10/GB-month, transfer billed separately). Artifactory/Nexus Pro bill storage AND data transfer combined as one consumption meter (~$0.90-1.10/GB for Nexus beyond an included tier) -- so high pull volume drives cost, not just stored data.

flashcards.q: What changed about ECR layer storage in January 2026?
flashcards.a: ECR now stores each unique layer once across all repositories in the same private registry (deduplicated), rather than storing shared base-image layers once per repository.

flashcards.q: What does Notary v2 continue as, and how does it compare to cosign/Sigstore's adoption?
flashcards.a: Notary v2 continues as the CNCF Notation project, a legitimate OCI-native signing spec, but cosign/Sigstore's keyless model and broader ecosystem adoption (Kyverno, Connaisseur) make it the more common default absent a specific reason to prefer Notation.

flashcards.q: Why does ECR need no imagePullSecrets for same-account EKS/ECS pulls, while Artifactory/Nexus typically does?
flashcards.a: ECR authenticates via the node's own IAM role (or Fargate task execution role) automatically. Artifactory/Nexus have no native AWS IAM integration and need an explicit imagePullSecrets Secret.

flashcards.q: What does a SLSA provenance attestation add beyond a valid image signature and SBOM attestation?
flashcards.a: Signature verification proves the artifact wasn't tampered with after signing by a known identity; SBOM attests contents. SLSA provenance is a separate signed claim about HOW the artifact was built (source commit, builder identity, build parameters) -- a build-process integrity guarantee neither of the other two provides.

flashcards.q: Why is ECR generally the wrong choice as a polyglot org's sole artifact registry?
flashcards.a: ECR is containers-only -- it doesn't handle Maven, npm, PyPI, or Helm artifacts, forcing a second tool anyway for non-container artifacts, at which point Artifactory/Nexus's single consumption-billed platform is usually the better consolidation.
